comment: Firewall-scope presets: which Bloated and risk recommendations apply for a kind of PC. role picks the knowledge-base role for Bloated; applyBloat disables the enabled Bloated rules (quick wins); risks lists the risk rule ids whose recommended fix applies (Keep and Ignore change nothing; protected, locked and Core Services rules are always skipped). Presets in data\presets name a scope with firewallScope.

scopes.name: Gaming PC
scopes.hint: Turns off sharing and remote-administration rules a gaming PC does not use and closes wide-open and public-network openings.
scopes.description: For a home gaming PC: disables the bloated Windows rules (legacy media sharing, remote administration, server features), removes rules of uninstalled programs and fixes inbound openings on public networks. Game, launcher and anti-cheat rules are never touched.

scopes.name: Workstation
scopes.hint: Keeps file and printer sharing and management for the office network; closes wide-open rules and public-network admin access.
scopes.description: For an office or domain PC: keeps sharing, discovery and device management, disables only legacy media sharing and similar bloat, and fixes wide-open rules, admin protocols on public networks and orphaned rules.

scopes.name: Public Wi-Fi laptop
scopes.hint: For laptops on hotel and cafe networks: nothing answers on public networks, local services only from the local subnet.
scopes.description: For a laptop that often joins untrusted networks: closes every inbound opening on the Public profile (sharing, discovery, remote access), limits local services to the local subnet, turns off edge traversal for apps and removes orphaned rules.

scopes.name: Sysadmin hardened
scopes.hint: Keeps remote administration but applies every Critical, High and Medium fix and removes consumer bloat.
scopes.description: For an administrator's PC: Remote Desktop, PowerShell remoting and WMI stay, consumer media sharing and casting go, and every critical, high and medium recommendation applies.
